The most notable pact made in 1761 was the third Pacte de Famille (Family Compact), concluded on 15 August 1761 by King Charles III of Spain and King Louis XV of France [d1][d7]. It was a defensive alliance between the two Bourbon monarchies during the Seven Years' War, and also included the Bourbon ruler of the Two Sicilies and the Infante Philip, duke of Parma [d4]. More broadly, the Pacte de Famille was one of three such alliances (1733, 1743, and 1761) between France and Spain, both ruled by members of the Bourbon family [d2]. Additionally, in February 1761, Spain and Portugal signed the Treaty of El Pardo, which repealed the earlier Treaty of Madrid of 1750 [d3], and a series of Peace and Friendship Treaties were also signed in 1760–1761 between Indigenous tribes (such as the "Jediack tribe of Indians") and the British government in Nova Scotia [d9].
